source.title: A Bayesian Perspective of Convolutional Neural Networks through a Deconvolutional Generative Model
source.authors: T. Nguyen; Nhat Ho; Ankit B. Patel; Anima Anandkumar; Michael I. Jordan; Richard Baraniuk

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a new regularizer (RPN) with the same model without RPN and reports test error on natural image datasets. This bears on whether an explicit regularizer changes generalization, but none of the listed versions specifically covers RPN.
record.gate_note: RPN comparisons are recorded as results about explicit regularization under fits_no_version; cited prior studies and the paper's generalization-bound arguments are not experimental rows. The dropout in the reported architecture is not ablated.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates RPN regularization and Max-Min cross-entropy and derives bounds involving active rendering paths. None tests V1–V8. Dropout, optimizer switching, convolutional architecture and batch size are recipe components without the comparisons those versions require.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' RPN conclusion: they describe small, consistent improvements across experiments. Their broader conclusion is that DGM provides a probabilistic framework for CNNs, theoretical guarantees and new training components, including Max-Min cross-entropy, that improve classification performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study introduces Rendering Path Normalization, a regularizer derived from its generative model, and evaluates it against DGM without RPN. The compared recipes are not the original interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and number of labeled training examples; the reported RPN gains vary in size across these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: RPN lowers reported mean test error across the recorded CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and SVHN comparisons after correcting table assignments; the CIFAR-10 gains are small, rather than the large reductions recorded in R1–R3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding RPN to DGM can improve image-classification test performance under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6.2 reports Max-Min cross-entropy reducing CIFAR-10 test error from 2.56% to 2.30% and ImageNet top-5 error from 7.21% to 7.04%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Max-Min cross-entropy can improve held-out classification performance over traditional cross-entropy for the tested convolutional models.

fits_no_version.finding: The theoretical generalization bound depends on the number of active rendering paths under specified assumptions; it does not measure weight-perturbation sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Active rendering-path complexity can enter a theoretical bound on DGM generalization.

record.problems: The paper reports ± values and multiple-run averages for many experiments, but does not clearly specify in the supplied text what the ± values represent. Some table layouts are flattened, making row-to-value assignment ambiguous, especially in Table 4. The experiment tests RPN rather than the claim versions' specified interventions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4's CIFAR-100, 10K-label DGM without-RPN and DGM+RPN pair is omitted because the flattened presentation does not support confident assignment of values. Other table entries compare Max-Min, Mean Teacher, or unrelated methods and do not isolate RPN's effect.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy under matched recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance and the effects of tuning or switching. The shared Adam-to-SGD schedule is not ablated.
Batch-size comparisons under matched epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including dataset-size, dropout-rate and augmentation conditions. Dropout is present without ablation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with generalization gaps and its ranking against other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row is outside those versions. These own-method comparisons should remain under fits_no_version, without claim verdicts. No additional result bearing on V1–V8 was identified in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local connectivity.
Large- versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout ablation and its effect across training-set sizes or dropout rates.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurement and its association with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.
